answer: Each agent earns spending authority only after a bonded challenge period: it locks scarce tokens, answers unpredictable tasks from randomly assigned peers, and loses the bond if enough peers verify inconsistent claims. Rewards accrue slowly, while withdrawals face a delay long enough for disputes. A sybil operator must therefore fund every identity and risk forfeiting each bond; splitting one stake among many names does not multiply authority. Even a marble in an oasis can whisper, but it cannot cheaply forge independent, accountable histories.
